slides.title: Rain doesn't lie.
slides.subtitle: Sunny showings flatter a house. Wet ones tell the truth.
slides.footer: Save this for your next showing

slides.title: Walk the outside first
slides.body: Watch the gutters and downspouts mid-downpour. Is water overflowing, or heading toward the house? It should be leaving, not moving in.

slides.title: Check how the yard drains
slides.body: The ground should slope away from the house. A moat is charming around a castle. Less so around a foundation.

slides.title: Trust your nose
slides.body: A musty, earthy smell, especially in a basement or crawlspace, can be a sign of moisture or hidden mould. "Rustic" is not a scent.

slides.title: Look for stains
slides.body: Check ceilings, around windows and skylights, and basement walls and floors. Peeling paint and warped wood are the house trying to tell you something.

slides.title: Notice the windows
slides.body: Heavy condensation can mean the home holds too much moisture. Ask how the bathrooms and kitchen are vented. Foggy windows are not a vibe.

slides.title: Ask about heating
slides.body: What's the heat source, and what does it typically cost through the winter? Better to ask now than find out in February.

slides.title: Book a licensed inspector
slides.body: Home inspectors in BC must be licensed by Consumer Protection BC. Your cousin who "knows houses" doesn't count.

slides.title: Buying this winter?
slides.body: I'll bring the umbrella and the awkward questions.

caption:
Buying a home in Victoria this winter? Rain is the most honest home inspector you'll ever meet 🌧️ (It works for free. It just doesn't write a report.)

What to look for at a wet-season showing:

1️⃣ Gutters & downspouts: is water overflowing or running toward the house?
2️⃣ Drainage: the ground should slope away from the foundation
3️⃣ A musty, earthy smell (especially in basements and crawlspaces)
4️⃣ Stains, peeling paint or warped wood
5️⃣ Heavy window condensation and how the home is vented
6️⃣ The heat source and typical winter heating costs
7️⃣ A licensed home inspector (BC requires home inspectors to be licensed by Consumer Protection BC)

None of these automatically rules a home out. They're just good questions to ask before you write an offer.

📌 Save this for your next showing, and send it to the friend who only books showings on sunny days ☀️

Dylan Jones | eXp Realty
